original_question: Within the paper's standard ansatz for classical de Sitter solutions in 10d type II supergravity - namely a 10d metric globally written as a 4d de Sitter space-time times a 6d compact manifold, with Op/Dp sources, then further restricted to smeared solutions on 6d compact group manifolds with constant fluxes - is there any classical de Sitter solution whose sources are parallel, meaning that the sources lie along the same dimensions in the 10d space-time, or must every such putative solution be excluded?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1 in the Introduction and section 3: "There is no classical de Sitter solution with parallel sources," understood in this paper through the precise ansatz of sections 2.1-2.2 (smeared solutions on 6d compact group manifolds with constant fluxes).
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual target. It correctly identifies that the paper is asking about classical de Sitter solutions of 10d type II supergravity, it includes the paper's working restriction to smeared solutions on compact 6d group manifolds with constant fluxes, and it uses the paper's intended meaning of "parallel sources" as sources lying along the same 10d directions.
missing_details: The stand-alone question should explicitly say that one is working in 10d type II supergravity with 4d-Lorentz-invariant BPS Op/Dp sources of a single size p >= 3, as assumed in section 2.1.

It should specify that the paper's operative ansatz is the smeared limit A = 0 of the metric/dilaton ansatz, on a compact 6d group manifold, with constant flux components in the flat basis, and no sources other than the Op/Dp sources.

It should state that the issue is existence of a full 10d solution, i.e. a background solving the Einstein equation, dilaton equation of motion, flux equations of motion, and Bianchi identities, not merely satisfying some traced equations or a 4d effective-potential extremality condition.
It should define "parallel sources" in the paper's own formalism as the case of a single set N = 1 of sources wrapping the same internal directions, as opposed to intersecting sources with N > 1.

To be paper-faithful, it should note that within this ansatz the only unresolved parallel-source cases are p = 4, 5, 6; earlier constraints summarized at the start of section 3 already exclude the other source dimensions.

The paper treats this as a conjecture/open problem rather than a theorem: section 3 develops further constraints but does not prove nonexistence, and section 3.3 plus section 6 explicitly say the conjecture remains open.

Ambient ring/field, homogeneity degree, nilpotency, and phrases like "for all sufficiently large m" are not relevant to this problem; the relevant variables to quantify over are instead the group-manifold structure constants, the orientifold-allowed constant flux components, and the source terms T10.
refined_question: Prove or disprove Conjecture 1 in the precise setting of sections 2.1-2.2 of arXiv:1902.10093: for 10d type II supergravity backgrounds with a globally defined 4d de Sitter factor and a compact 6d internal group manifold, 4d-Lorentz-invariant BPS Op/Dp sources of a single size p >= 3, and in the smeared limit A = 0 with constant internal flux components in the flat basis subject to the orientifold projection, does there exist any solution of the full 10d equations of motion and Bianchi identities with one set N = 1 of parallel sources (equivalently, all sources wrap the same internal directions), or must no such classical de Sitter solution exist?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, because the earlier no-go constraints summarized at the start of section 3 already remove all other source dimensions in this ansatz, one may ask: can any of the remaining p = 4, 5, 6 parallel-source cases solve the full 10d equations and Bianchi identities, or are even those cases impossible?
justification: The nearest official formulation is Conjecture 1 in the Introduction: "There is no classical de Sitter solution with parallel sources" (section 1, p. 3). The paper then makes that statement precise only after imposing the detailed ansatz of sections 2.1-2.2: 10d type II backgrounds with a 4d de Sitter factor, compact 6d internal space, 4d-Lorentz-invariant BPS Op/Dp sources of one size, then the smeared A = 0 group-manifold and constant-flux restrictions, together with the remaining 10d equations and Bianchi identities to solve (pp. 4-8). Section 3 is exactly the analysis of this conjecture for parallel sources, and its opening paragraph states that only p = 4, 5, 6 remain as possible cases within the ansatz (p. 9). Section 3.3 and the summary in section 6 show that the conjecture is still open rather than proved, even in a simplified p = 6 corner (pp. 15-16, 29-30). So the refined question should be a sharply scoped existence/nonexistence question for full 10d solutions with N = 1 parallel sources, not a broader or differently framed problem.
